newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Monday, as traders expected a quiet start to the week with LIFFE closed for a bank holiday.
Some dealers said the market was likely to trade sideways, consolidating Friday's losses.
"On Friday we got a lot people out who were nervous," one trader said. "Now, I think we can try to find a stable price."

Friday, New York arabica futures ended in sharply lower in a technical correction to the market's recent steep upswing. July fell 6.75 cents per lb, to 216.15 cents, after ranging between a new lifetime high of 225.00 and 211.50 cents. Spot May settled down 5.20 cents, to 247.55,while the back months closed 1.90 to 5.85 lower.
Technically, traders pegged near-term support was at the Friday's low of 211.50 basis July and said a breach of that level could lead to a test of the psychologically crucial $2 mark.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 750 bags, to 42,918 bags as of May 1. There here were 10,477 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
German trade house Bernard Rothfos said Brazil's 1997/98 coffe crop is likely to come 15-20 percent below the previous season's harvest at between 24 and 25.5 million 60-kg bags.
In its quarterly report, Rothfos revised upward its 1996/97 Brazil estimate to 30 million bags from 27 million bags forecast in January.
The London coffee market will reopen on Tuesday.
